meta.description: Tests ranked gene vectors for coordinated pathway shifts and scores per-sample pathway activity.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

scientific_integrity.detail: All numeric claims used for scoring were produced by saved synthetic runs; no fabricated biomedical findings were presented.

practice_boundaries.detail: The Skill analyzes pathway statistics and makes no patient-specific diagnostic or treatment recommendation.

methodological_ground.detail: The Skill distinguishes correlation-sensitive preranked screening from CAMERA and required ID, sorting, seed, and multiple-testing controls executed as documented.

code_usability.detail: All seven fresh regression inputs completed with exit 0 in the documented isolated runtime.

functional_suitability.note: GO, KEGG, Reactome, MSigDB, CAMERA/fry, GSVA, and ssGSEA claims each have an applicable route.

reliability.note: Strong validation and failure-mode guidance; live KEGG availability and factor-level orientation require user attention.

performance_context.note: The 252-line Skill is dense but bounded and identifies the expensive GO run and live KEGG dependency.

agent_usability.note: Decision tree, input requirements, warnings, and report fields are explicit; contrast orientation needs one explicit line.

human_usability.note: Natural prompts and short usage guide are present; the advanced statistical content remains necessarily technical.

security.note: No credentials, destructive operations, or untrusted-code execution are documented.

maintainability.note: Version block is a single source of truth and examples are present; runtime setup is substantial.

agent_specific.note: Trigger description and escape hatches are precise; the main file has no reference split but remains below the 300-line repository threshold.

The Skill explicitly guards ranking order, duplicate IDs, ID mismatch, nPerm fallback, seed use, and correlated-gene inference.
The version block now treats a nonzero process exit as a failed computation rather than accepting printed output.

recommendations.title: Make case/control coefficient orientation explicit
recommendations.problem: The Matrix + Design snippet invokes model.matrix(~ group) without fixing the reference level, so a default lexical factor order can invert the advertised case-versus-control Direction.
recommendations.root_cause: The example describes factor values but does not construct or relevel the factor before selecting coefficient 2.
recommendations.fix: Set group <- factor(group, levels = c('Control', 'Case')) before model.matrix(~ group), and state that Direction is relative to the resulting Case-versus-Control coefficient.
